question: For $x>1$, differentiate $$y=(\log x)^{\log x}$$ with respect to $x$.
explanation:
Taking logarithm
Given $$y=(\log x)^{\log x},$$ taking logarithm gives $$\log y=(\log x)\log(\log x).$$
Differentiation
$$\frac{1}{y}\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{1}{x}\log(\log x)+(\log x)\frac{1}{x\log x}.$$
Simplifying, $$\frac{1}{y}\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{\log(\log x)+1}{x}.$$
Substitution of the original function
Hence, $$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{(\log x)^{\log x}}{x}\left[1+\log(\log x)\right].$$
